arxiv-1907-05552.title: Tiny-Inception-ResNet-v2: Using Deep Learning for Eliminating Bonded Labors of Brick Kilns in South Asia
arxiv-1907-05552.creator: Usman Nazir, Numan Khurshid, Muhammad Ahmed Bhimra, Murtaza Taj
arxiv-1907-05552.description: Abstract This paper proposes to employ a Inception-ResNet inspired deep learning architecture called Tiny-Inception-ResNet-v2 to eliminate bonded labor by identifying brick kilns within ‘‘Brick-Kiln-Belt’’ of South Asia. The framework is developed by training a network on the satellite imagery consisting of 11 different classes of South Asian region.

arxiv-2105-14038.title: Learning to Extend Program Graphs to Work-in-Progress Code
arxiv-2105-14038.creator: Xuechen Li, Chris J. Maddison, Daniel Tarlow
arxiv-2105-14038.description: Abstract Source code spends most of its time in a broken or incomplete state during software development. This presents a challenge to machine learning for code, since high-performing models typically rely on graph structured representations of programs derived from traditional program analyses. Such analyses may be undefined for broken or incomplete code.

arxiv-2106-12295.title: Quantum Brain Networks: a Perspective
arxiv-2106-12295.creator: E. R. Miranda, S. Venkatesh, C. Hernani-Morales, L. Lamata, J. D. Martín-Guerrero, E. Solano
arxiv-2106-12295.description: Abstract We propose Quantum Brain Networks (QBraiNs) as a new interdisciplinary field integrating knowledge and methods from neurotechnology, artificial intelligence, and quantum computing. The objective is to develop an enhanced connectivity between the human brain and quantum computers for a variety of disruptive applications.

arxiv-2108-06348.title: The cumulative hierarchy in Homotopy Type Theory
arxiv-2108-06348.creator: Ioannis Eleftheriadis
arxiv-2108-06348.description: Abstract We explore the cumulative hierarchy V V defined in Chapter 10 of the HoTT book. We begin by showing how to translate formulas of set theory in HoTT, and proceed to examine which axioms are satisfied in V V .

arxiv-2211-08710.title: Missing odd-order Shapiro steps do not uniquely indicate fractional Josephson effect
arxiv-2211-08710.creator: P. Zhang, S. Mudi, M. Pendharkar, J.S. Lee, C.P. Dempsey, A.P. McFadden, S.D. Harrington, J.T. Dong, H. Wu, A.-H. Chen, M. Hocevar, C.J. Palmstrøm, S.M. Frolov
arxiv-2211-08710.description: Abstract Topological superconductivity is expected to spur Majorana zero modes—exotic states that are also considered a quantum technology asset. Fractional Josephson effect is their manifestation in electronic transport measurements, often under microwave irradiation. A fraction of induced resonances, known as Shapiro steps, should vanish, in a pattern that signifies the presence of Majorana modes.

arxiv-2309-03245.title: Testing properties of distributions in the streaming model
arxiv-2309-03245.creator: Sampriti Roy, Yadu Vasudev
arxiv-2309-03245.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sampriti Roy, Yadu Vasudev. We study distribution testing in the standard access model and the conditional access model when the memory available to the testing algorithm is bounded. In both scenarios, the samples appear in an online fashion and the goal is to test the properties of distribution using an optimal number of samples subject to a memory constraint on how many samples can be stored at a given time.

arxiv-2506-10172.title: A Navigation Framework Utilizing Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2506-10172.creator: Yicheng Duan, Kaiyu Tang
arxiv-2506-10172.description: Abstract Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) presents a complex challenge in embodied AI, requiring agents to interpret natural language instructions and navigate through visually rich, unfamiliar environments. Recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs), such as CLIP and Flamingo, have significantly improved multimodal understanding but introduced new challenges related to computational cost and real-time deployment.

pmc-10648680.title: Electronic, Optical, and Vibrational Properties of an AgAlS2 Crystal in a High-Pressure Phase
pmc-10648680.creator: Myron Ya. Rudysh, Anatolii O. Fedorchuk, Mikhail G. Brik, Jurij Grechenkov, Dmitry Bocharov, Sergei Piskunov, Anatoli I. Popov, Michal Piasecki
pmc-10648680.description: The aim of this study is to comprehensively examine the structural composition and properties of the AgAlS2 crystal during its high-pressure phase. This analysis delves into the second coordination environment of the crystal structure and elucidates the distinct transformations it undergoes during the phase transition. The band energy structure was calculated, and the origin of electronic levels was clarified.

pmc-12392435.title: Making weight makes sense: relative performance gains after rapid weight loss in powerlifting: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-12392435.creator: Arkadiusz Matras, Michał Czapla, Artur Struzik
pmc-12392435.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundRapid weight loss (RWL) is a common strategy among competitive powerlifters aiming to qualify for lower weight categories and improve competitive advantage. However, the effects of RWL followed by short-term recovery on maximal strength performance remain unclear. This study aimed to examine whether a ~ 5% RWL protocol followed by a 2-hour recovery period affects changes in maximal and relative strength performance in trained male powerlifters.MethodsThis randomized controlled trial (RCT) was registered in the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN12622000924752).

pmc-12446291.title: Impact of ERAP1 downregulation on the pathogenesis of DSS-induced colitis and therapeutic response to sulfasalazine
pmc-12446291.creator: Bushra Riaz, Hye-Myung Ryu, S. M. Shamsul Islam, Rahar Babita, Je Kyung Seong, Ho Lee, Eunjoo H. Lee, Seonghyang Sohn
pmc-12446291.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionUlcerative colitis (UC) is a life-threatening heterogeneous condition characterized by inflammation of the colon. Endoplasmic reticulum aminopeptidase 1 (ERAP1) is essential for antigen processing and immune regulation, however, its specific role in UC pathogenesis and therapeutic response remains unclear.

pmc-12641050.title: White Blood Cells in Neurodegenerative Diseases in the Context of Neuroinflammation
pmc-12641050.creator: Agnieszka Wełnicka-Wesołowska, Monika Gołąb-Janowska
pmc-12641050.description: Neurodegenerative diseases are a multifactorial problem for modern neurology, due to their unknown etiology, difficult diagnostics, and, consequently, the lack of causal methods of treatment. Rising life expectancy exacerbates the problem by increasing the number of patients, as most of them fall ill in older age.

pmc-12733034.title: Synergistic Effects of High-Intensity Interval Training and Asparagus officinalis L. Root Extract Supplementation on Metabolic Regulation, Oxidative Stress, and Inflammation in Overweight and Obese Adults
pmc-12733034.creator: Piyapong Prasertsri, Tadsawiya Padkao, Orachorn Boonla, Surachat Buddhisa, Nattaphol Prakobkaew, Siriporn Sripinyowanich, Jatuporn Phoemsapthawee, Bruno Eto
pmc-12733034.description: Excess adiposity is associated with increased oxidative stress and inflammation, which contribute to metabolic dysregulation. Both exercise training and bioactive plant-derived compounds have been explored as therapeutic strategies to mitigate these effects. Asparagus (Asparagus officinalis L.) root extract, rich in ecdysteroids such as 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E), exhibits potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities.

pmc-13556111.title: War trauma and psychomotor developmental disorders in children aged 6–12 in Lubumbashi: a comparative study
pmc-13556111.creator: Joëlle Ngoie Musasa, Malko Ibrahim, Philippe Kaganda, Adélaïde Blavier, Jennifer Foucart
pmc-13556111.description: Background: Persistent armed conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has resulted in large-scale population displacement, exposing many children to traumatic experiences. Although the psychological consequences of such exposure are well documented, its impact on psychomotor development remains insufficiently investigated, particularly in African settings affected by chronic violence.

pmc-13564396.title: Rooting plant awareness: development of a tool to explore human-plant relationships
pmc-13564396.creator: Benno Dünser, Ivo Ponocny, Francisco Javier Navarro Prieto, Peter Lampert, Peter Pany
pmc-13564396.description: BackgroundAlthough plants play a crucial role in ecosystems and human well-being, public awareness of their ecological significance remains limited. Furthermore, no validated construct or instrument currently exists to systematically assess plant awareness.MethodsThis study presents an operationalisation and statistical validation of the plant awareness construct through a newly-developed assessment tool.
